docs.title: IMU-Bench
docs.text:
Benchmarking wrist IMU representations across kinematic, semantic and clinical tasks.

IMU-Bench evaluates one wrist-IMU encoder on ten tasks from eight datasets: arm and full-body pose, inertial odometry, microgesture recognition, IMU–text retrieval, Parkinson's disease classification and activity recognition on four sets. Every task is defined by a task card that fixes the raw input, the decoder, the training recipe, the split, the selection rule and the scorer, so that the encoder is the only thing that differs between rows of the leaderboard. The benchmark ships with InrtlWrist, a general-purpose inertial foundation model for wrist-worn IMUs, and with the per-cell result files behind every number in the paper.

Website and leaderboard Code InrtlWrist weights Results and submissions Paper: arXiv:2610.19481

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
• One harness, one protocol. imu-bench eval trains and scores every encoder with the same decoders, splits, budgets and scorers; nothing on the leaderboard is typed by hand.
  • Two submission paths. Plug any PyTorch encoder in through a small interface, or register an encoder trained with the shared backbone for the controlled track.
  • Audited data. Every evaluation set was checked for duplicated participants and for overlap with common pretraining pools before it was split; submissions declare their corpus and are checked the same way.
  • Open results. Each cell of the leaderboard is one JSON file with all metrics, the selected checkpoint and the exact config; submissions are pull requests that carry the same artefacts.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/SPICExLAB/IMU-Bench && cd IMU-Bench
python -m venv imu-bench && source imu-bench/bin/activate && pip install -e .
export IMUBENCH_DATA_ROOT=/data/imubench           # see Datasets
imu-bench tasks                                    # the ten task cards
imu-bench eval --encoder examples/plugin/inrtlwrist_plugin.yaml --tasks har_hhar --protocols probe

import torch
from huggingface_hub import hf_hub_download
from scripts.load_inrtlwrist import load_inrtlwrist, zscore

enc = load_inrtlwrist(hf_hub_download("YiquanLi/InrtlWrist", "inrtlwrist_mae_5src_step144k.pt"))
z = enc(zscore(torch.randn(2, 6, 512)))            # [2, 384] pooled embedding of two 10.24 s wrist windows

docs.title: FAQ
docs.text:
My model only uses the accelerometer. Set channels: 3 in the encoder card; the gyroscope channels are dropped before your model. The row is marked accelerometer-only on the leaderboard.

My model expects 30 Hz input and 10 s windows. Set model_hz: 30; the harness resamples (anti-aliased when downsampling). Window lengths are fixed by the task cards (1 s to 10.24 s); a model that needs longer context sees the task window only.

My model normalises its own input. Set normalize_method: raw and do it inside forward. The benchmark fixes the raw input, not the normalisation; the released encoders use per-window z-scoring, physical-unit and raw inputs are supported as well.

Can I tune the probe or the fine-tuning recipe? No. The decoder, learning rate, budget and selection rule belong to the task card; imu-bench check compares every trained config with the card, and a cell that changed them is listed outside the ranking. Fine-tuning is the protocol for showing what the encoder reaches with adaptation.

Can I submit embeddings instead of an encoder? Not at the moment; see Submission modes.

I only ran some tasks. imu-bench package --allow-incomplete lays the results out and the pull request is accepted, but the row is not ranked until all twenty cells (ten tasks × two protocols) exist.

How long does a full run take? On one A100, a few hours for the twenty cells of a 21 M-parameter encoder; the kinematic fine-tunes dominate.

A reference row does not reproduce the released number. Check the data preparation first (Datasets); the reference rows control_random, control_raw, scratch and mae_5src exist so that a setup can be verified before a new model is trusted.

Which seed? 42 for every cell on the leaderboard. Differences inside the measurement noise are not separated; the paper reports the noise band of the kinematic tasks and bold marks ties at the printed precision.

Why is the leaderboard regenerated instead of edited? So that every number traces to a result file with its checkpoint step and config. imu-bench leaderboard rebuilds the tables from bench/results/.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/SPICExLAB/IMU-Bench && cd IMU-Bench
python -m venv imu-bench && source imu-bench/bin/activate
pip install -e .
imu-bench tasks

Python 3.9 or newer and one GPU. Install the CUDA build of PyTorch first if pip picks the CPU wheel for your platform; every run in the paper used one NVIDIA A100 or H100.

The install is editable because the harness runs inside the clone:

Path Holds configs/ task templates and pretraining configs bench/registry/ task cards, encoder cards, protocols, tracks bench/generated/configs/ the generated config of every cell (the paper's are committed) runs/ training runs: checkpoints and logs, one directory per cell bench/results/ one result JSON per cell

SLURM

imu-bench eval --slurm submits one train → score chain per cell. The generated scripts activate imu-bench/ by default; set IMUBENCH_VENV to use another environment directory, and BENCH_PARTITION / BENCH_ACCOUNT for your queue.

Next: Quickstart, then Datasets.

docs.title: Roadmap
docs.text:
Planned, in rough order:

  • Lite subset. One task per family with a one-GPU-hour budget, for development runs.
  • Docker image. An official image with pinned dependencies, and the requirement that leaderboard runs use it.
  • Spot re-runs. Every open-track submission with public weights re-run on a sample of cells, with the outcome reported on the pull request.
  • Embeddings mode. A frozen-probe-only path for the global tasks, listed outside the ranking, for models whose weights cannot be released.
  • Data. The Nymeria preprocessing converter, the TransfHAR release and the regenerated HumanML3D wrist simulation (see the gaps in Datasets).
  • Multi-seed rows for the leaderboard's top entries.

docs.title: Tasks
docs.text: Ten tasks from eight datasets, in six families. Every task reads the same input, one wrist's accelerometer and gyroscope in a forward–left–up frame, and is defined by a task card that fixes the window, the decoder, the training recipe, the split, the selection rule and the scorer (see Task cards). The figures below show, for each family, the input window, what the encoder and the card's decoder produce, and how it is scored. Input traces are real Nymeria right-wrist windows; labels, captions and class scores are illustrative.

docs.title: Pose estimation
docs.text:
Arm pose arm_pose_nymeria Full-body pose full_body_pose_nymeria Dataset Nymeria: real right-wrist IMU with Project-Aria motion capture, 300 h released same Input 10.24 s window at 50 Hz same Output 6-D rotations of the five right-arm joints (collar, shoulder, elbow, wrist, hand) per 0.32 s patch 6-D rotations of the 23 SMPL body joints per 0.32 s patch; the pelvis orientation comes from ground truth Decoder width-192 attention decoder, two cross-channel and two temporal layers width-192 attention decoder, one cross-channel layer Metric forward-kinematics position error of the five joints, cm ↓ root-relative MPJPE over the 23 joints, mm ↓ Split by recording session (867 training, 101 evaluation sessions); participants recur same

Frozen features trail training from scratch on full-body pose; fine-tuning InrtlWrist reaches 88.1 mm against 92.7 mm from scratch.

docs.title: Inertial odometry
docs.text:
Inertial odometry odometry_nymeria_local Dataset Nymeria (same recordings as the pose tasks) Input 2.56 s window at 50 Hz Output pelvis velocity in the wrist frame, four values per 0.32 s patch Decoder width-192 attention decoder, one temporal layer Scoring the predicted velocities are rotated into the world frame with the ground-truth initial wrist orientation propagated by integrating the gyroscope, summed into a trajectory and compared with the pelvis trajectory: absolute trajectory error, m ↓ Split by recording session

The protocol uses the true initial orientation and short windows, so it is easier than full inertial navigation and its numbers are not comparable to world-frame odometry systems. Fine-tuned InrtlWrist reaches 0.154 m ATE against 0.162 m from scratch.

docs.title: Microgesture recognition
docs.text:
Microgesture microgesture_openwatch Dataset OpenWatch: five hand gestures (double clench, double pinch, pinch down, pinch up, slide) plus background, real recordings Input 1 s windows at 100 Hz, six windows per clip from a centred 2 s interval Output class logits per window; a clip is labelled by the first run of three identical window predictions, else by majority Decoder linear head Metric clip macro-F1 on the test split ↑ Split by participant over the 43 canonical identities (the release's 50 ids contain duplicated and mirrored recordings), stratified by posture

Frozen InrtlWrist reaches 64.7 clip F1 and stays ahead of every fine-tuned matched method on this task.

docs.title: IMU–text retrieval
docs.text:
IMU–text retrieval language_humanml3d Dataset HumanML3D motions with right-wrist IMU simulated from the motion capture (UniMTS release), with captions Input 10.24 s window at 50 Hz Output an embedding aligned with the CLIP ViT-B/32 text space Decoder a projection, trained with paired motion–text supervision for every encoder alike Metric mean Recall@1 over IMU→text and text→IMU in galleries of 100 (200 random galleries on the official test split; the full gallery holds 3,701 clips) ↑ Split the official HumanML3D split; 437 of the test clips share source frames with training clips, which affects every encoder equally

All encoders receive paired supervision during downstream training, so the task measures how well a pretrained representation supports learning alignment, not zero-shot alignment. Under frozen probing no supervised source task approaches the pretrained encoder here (27.9 Recall@1).

docs.title: Parkinson's disease classification
docs.text:
Parkinson's disease pd_pads Dataset PADS (PhysioNet): 469 participants, healthy control, Parkinson's disease or differential diagnosis; eleven scripted assessment steps recorded on both wrists Input 2.56 s windows at 50 Hz; each (participant, step, wrist) recording is its own single-wrist session Output class logits per window; a participant's prediction is the argmax of the mean posterior over all of that participant's windows Decoder linear head, inverse-frequency class-weighted cross-entropy Metric participant macro-F1 over the three classes ↑ (balanced accuracy is reported too) Split subject-disjoint 80/20 (375 / 94 participants)

The participant metric is coarse: a never-trained frozen encoder reaches 51.7, so encoders within a few points of each other are not separated by it.

docs.title: Activity recognition
docs.text:
HHAR har_hhar MHEALTH har_mhealth PrISM har_prism TransfHAR har_userwatch Classes 6 12 5 global daily-living procedures 60 everyday hand activities Subjects 9 10 31 10 Split subject-disjoint, 20 % held out subject-disjoint, 20 % held out subject-disjoint, 20 % held out 80/20 in time within each recording, since most activities were performed by one participant

All four use 2.56 s windows at 50 Hz, a linear head and window macro-F1 ↑; the leaderboard's activity column is the mean over the four sets. These sets are held out of the released pretraining corpus; the activity datasets that are in the corpus (WISDM, PAMAP2, RecoFit, SAMoSA, UT-Watch) appear in the website's per-task table for reference only.

docs.title: Data audit and leakage
docs.text: Every evaluation set went through two audits before it was split, and every submission is checked the same way.

docs.title: Declare the pretraining corpus
docs.text:
The encoder card lists the pretraining corpus dataset by dataset, with the split used (pretrain_data). The evaluation splits of the ten tasks must not be in it. Declare bundles by their member datasets: common activity-recognition pools contain WISDM, PAMAP2, RecoFit, SAMoSA, Shoaib and UT-Watch, which is why those sets are not evaluation tasks here and why the four activity tasks (HHAR, MHEALTH, PrISM, TransfHAR) are held out of the released corpus.

Overlap Meaning Leaderboard none the corpus contains no recording of any evaluation split ranked exposure unlabeled evaluation recordings were in the pretraining corpus listed as overlap, not ranked on the affected tasks leakage evaluation participants or labels were used for training not listed

docs.title: Audit a release before splitting it
docs.text:
imu-bench audit <dir> --subject-regex 'id_(\d+)/' [--glob '**/*.csv'] [--acc-cols AccX AccY AccZ]
  1. Exact copies. Every file is hashed; identical files under different participant ids link those ids.
  2. Mirrored or rotated copies (with --acc-cols). The accelerometer magnitude is unchanged by mirroring or rotating the sensor axes, so two recordings whose standardised magnitude correlates above 0.999 at a small lag are the same motion.

Linked ids are merged into identity groups; a participant-disjoint split must be made over these groups. On OpenWatch this reduces 50 participant ids to 43 people and links all 35 motion-augmented ids to their sources, which is the procedure behind the benchmark's gesture split.

docs.title: Five checks for any wrist-IMU evaluation
docs.text:
1. Hash a release before splitting it by participant (above).
  2. Check the pretraining pool against every evaluation set. An earlier corpus of ours contained Nymeria and HumanML3D training splits and OpenWatch recordings; the released corpus does not.
  3. Run a never-trained encoder through the same decoder. The control_random and control_raw rows show what the decoder alone achieves; with a 12-layer odometry decoder the untrained encoder beats every pretrained one.
  4. Verify sensor units for every source. EatingSpeed stores the gyroscope in deg/s and OpenWatch stores raw counts; the harness converts units on load and rejects a source whose still windows have a median gyroscope magnitude above 0.3 rad/s.
  5. Know when an official split is partly transductive. 437 of HumanML3D's 2,192 test clips share frames with a training or validation clip; this affects every encoder equally and is stated with the retrieval results.

docs.title: Getting the data
docs.text:
IMU-Bench does not redistribute any dataset. Every evaluation set has to be downloaded from its source under that source's licence. This page gives the access steps (checked on 2026-10-14), the licence, the files the harness reads, and the directory layout it expects.

Gates at a glance. No dataset needs a signed data-use agreement or a credentialed account. Three need a free registration, and the rest download directly.

Task(s) Dataset Licence Access Arm pose, full-body pose, odometry Nymeria CC BY-NC 4.0 email sign-up; download links expire after 14 days Full-body pose (scorer) SMPL body model SMPL-Model licence (non-commercial) registration Microgesture OpenWatch CC BY 4.0 Hugging Face login + automatic gate IMU–text retrieval HumanML3D + AMASS MIT (texts) / AMASS research licence AMASS registration Parkinson's PADS (PhysioNet) CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 open access, no account Activity HHAR, MHEALTH (UCI) CC BY 4.0 direct download Activity PrISM see below partly public Activity TransfHAR (ours) — release in preparation

Some sets are only partly public, and the TransfHAR release is still in preparation. See Known gaps before planning a full run.

docs.title: Directory layout
docs.text:
The task cards name our cluster's paths. Put the data under one directory with the layout below and set IMUBENCH_DATA_ROOT to it. Every dataset path in the registry and in the generated configs is then rewritten to that directory.

$IMUBENCH_DATA_ROOT/
  processed_data_body_Ty_rwrist/          Nymeria training recordings, one *_cpfbody_rwrist_imu50hz_wristimu50hz_pose50hz.pkl each (867)
  processed_data_test_body_Ty_rwrist/     Nymeria evaluation recordings (101)
  openwatch_raw/open_watch_without_augmentations/
  HumanML3D/                              HumanML3D texts + UniMTS_data/data/{sim,aug_texts}
  pads_dataset.parquet                    scripts/prepare_pads_dataset.py
  hhar_dataset.parquet                    scripts/prepare_hhar_dataset.py
  mhealth_dataset.parquet                 scripts/prepare_mhealth_dataset.py
  userstudy_watch_dataset.parquet         scripts/prepare_userstudy_watch.py (TransfHAR)
  IMULM_master_dataset_v2.parquet         PrISM, in the shared activity schema

export IMUBENCH_DATA_ROOT=/data/imubench
imu-bench eval --encoder my_encoder.yaml

Two further paths are repo-relative and stay inside the clone: assets/smpl/basicmodel_m.pkl (the SMPL model) and the HF cache for the CLIP text tower used by the retrieval task.

docs.title: Nymeria (arm pose, full-body pose, odometry)
docs.text:
• Source: https://www.projectaria.com/datasets/nymeria/, code at https://github.com/facebookresearch/nymeria_dataset. The original release is on the nymeria_dataset_legacy branch; main now holds NymeriaPlus.
  • Licence: CC BY-NC 4.0. Derived data may be shared for non-commercial use, with attribution.
  • Access:
  • Enter your email under "Access the Dataset" on the project page. This accepts the licence and opens the download page.
  • Download the URL file there, or build a filtered one in the explorer (https://explorer.projectaria.com/nymeria).
  • Run download.py -i <urls.json> -o <out> from the Nymeria repository. The links expire after 14 days; fetch a new URL file when they do. The files are personal signed URLs, so never commit them.
  • What the benchmark needs: two data groups per sequence. Skip the head, observer and video groups; the full dataset is about 70 TB.
  • body_motion: body/xdata.npz, the XSens ground truth, about 1.1 TB.
  • recording_rwrist: recording_rwrist/data/motion.vrs and mps/slam/closed_loop_trajectory.csv, about 0.5 TB.
  • Cite: Ma et al., Nymeria: A Massive Collection of Multimodal Egocentric Daily Motion in the Wild, ECCV 2024.

docs.title: SMPL (full-body pose scorer)
docs.text:
• Source: https://smpl.is.tue.mpg.de/. Register, download "SMPL for Python", and place the male model at assets/smpl/basicmodel_m.pkl (see assets/smpl/README.md).
  • Licence: SMPL-Model licence, non-commercial scientific research. The model files may not be redistributed.

docs.title: OpenWatch (microgesture)
docs.text:
• Source: https://huggingface.co/datasets/pietrobonazzi/openwatch
  • Licence: CC BY 4.0.
  • Access: log in to Hugging Face, accept the gate (approved automatically), then huggingface-cli download --repo-type dataset pietrobonazzi/openwatch.
  • What the benchmark needs: only open_watch_without_augmentations/. In the augmented release, participants 51–85 are mirrored copies of real participants. The CSVs hold raw sensor counts; the task card converts them to m/s² and rad/s.
  • Cite: Bonazzi, Ahmed et al., OpenWatch: A Multimodal Benchmark for Hand Gesture Recognition on Smartwatches, arXiv:2605.04791.

docs.title: HumanML3D (IMU–text retrieval)
docs.text:
• Source: https://github.com/EricGuo5513/HumanML3D (code and texts, MIT). The motion comes from AMASS (https://amass.is.tue.mpg.de/), which needs a registration and allows no redistribution of the data or of anything derived from it.
  • Access:
  • Register at AMASS, and download the SMPL+H G archives together with SMPL+H and DMPL.
  • Run the HumanML3D scripts to rebuild the motions, texts and official train/val/test.txt splits.
  • Simulated wrist IMU: the task reads simulated right-wrist IMU and caption paraphrases in the UniMTS format, UniMTS_data/data/sim/<id>.npy and UniMTS_data/data/aug_texts/<id>.txt (UniMTS, https://github.com/xiyuanzh/UniMTS). These two folders are not in the public UniMTS_data.zip on Hugging Face. See Known gaps.
  • Cite: Guo et al., CVPR 2022; Mahmood et al., AMASS, ICCV 2019; Zhang et al., UniMTS, NeurIPS 2024.

docs.title: PADS (Parkinson's disease)
docs.text:
• Source: https://physionet.org/content/parkinsons-disease-smartwatch/1.0.0/
  • Licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0. Open access: the PhysioNet page reads "Anyone can access the files". No account, training course or data-use agreement is needed.
  • Access: download the ZIP, or wget -r -N -c -np https://physionet.org/files/parkinsons-disease-smartwatch/1.0.0/, then run python scripts/prepare_pads_dataset.py.
  • Cite: Varghese et al., Machine learning in the Parkinson's disease smartwatch (PADS) dataset, npj Parkinson's Disease 10, 9 (2024).

docs.title: HHAR and MHEALTH (activity)
docs.text:
• Sources: https://archive.ics.uci.edu/dataset/344 (HHAR) and https://archive.ics.uci.edu/dataset/319 (MHEALTH), both CC BY 4.0, direct download.
  • Build: python scripts/prepare_hhar_dataset.py (reads Watch_accelerometer.csv / Watch_gyroscope.csv) and python scripts/prepare_mhealth_dataset.py.
  • Cite: Stisen et al., SenSys 2015; Banos et al., IWAAL 2014.

docs.title: PrISM (activity)
docs.text:
• Source: the PrISM procedure-tracking recordings of Arakawa, Goel et al. (CMU), https://github.com/cmusmashlab/prism. The repository is MIT-licensed; whether that licence covers the data is not stated.
  • What the task uses: 31 participants and 16.3 h over eight procedures. The five classes are our grouping of the procedure steps into activities of daily living (food, household, personal care, appliance, desk/device).
  • Availability: the public download (Dropbox, linked from the repository) holds the cooking and latte_making sessions, about 5.2 of the 16.3 h. See Known gaps.
  • Cite: Arakawa et al., PrISM-Tracker, Proc. ACM IMWUT 6(4), 2022.

docs.title: TransfHAR (activity)
docs.text: Sixty activities recorded with a smartwatch for this paper. Its release is in preparation; until then the task cannot be run outside our group.

docs.title: Pretraining corpus (controlled track only)
docs.text:
Only controlled-track submissions retrain on the IMU-Bench corpus; open-track submissions bring their own weights.

Source Where Licence WISDM 2019 https://archive.ics.uci.edu/dataset/507 CC BY 4.0 RecoFit https://github.com/microsoft/Exercise-Recognition-from-Wearable-Sensors (git lfs pull) CDLA-Permissive-2.0 PAMAP2 https://archive.ics.uci.edu/dataset/231 CC BY 4.0 SAMoSA https://github.com/cmusmashlab/SAMoSA CMU non-commercial research licence (no redistribution) Shoaib (complex activities) https://www.utwente.nl/en/eemcs/ps/research/dataset/ no licence stated; cite Shoaib et al., Sensors 2016 UT-Watch https://doi.org/10.18738/T8/NNDFQD CC0 1.0 OCDetect https://zenodo.org/records/13924901 CC BY 4.0 EatingSpeed https://rdr.kuleuven.be/dataset.xhtml?persistentId=doi:10.48804/CN8VBB CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 (no sharing of adapted data) Motion-X++ https://huggingface.co/datasets/YuhongZhang/Motion-Xplusplus Motion-X licence (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 + per-subset licences) BONES-SEED https://huggingface.co/datasets/bones-studio/seed (scripts/download/download_bones_seed.py) BONES-SEED licence (gated; no public re-upload; attribution required)

Caches are built with scripts/build_multidata_cache.py --config configs/base.yaml --model-config <pretrain config> --out-dir <cache dir>. Because of the EatingSpeed, SAMoSA, AMASS and BONES-SEED terms, the built cache cannot be shared as a file.

docs.title: Known gaps
docs.text:
We are working on each of these. Until they are closed, a third party can run 7 of the 10 tasks end to end: arm pose, full-body pose, odometry, microgesture, Parkinson's, HHAR and MHEALTH.

  • IMU–text retrieval. The simulated wrist IMU and caption paraphrases (UniMTS_data/data/{sim,aug_texts}) are not in the public UniMTS download, and they derive from AMASS, so we cannot redistribute our copy. You can regenerate them with the UniMTS pipeline (pos2bvh.py, then IMUSim bvh2ts.py, then text_aug.py). The paraphrases are written by a language model, so a regenerated set will not match ours exactly.
  • PrISM. Only two of the eight procedures are in the public download.
  • TransfHAR. Release in preparation.
  • Nymeria preprocessing. The converter from the raw Nymeria groups to the per-recording .pkl files is not in this repository yet.

docs.title: Running cells
docs.text:
imu-bench eval --encoder my_encoder.yaml                        # registers the card, then all 20 cells, here
imu-bench eval --encoder my_encoder --tasks har_hhar pd_pads --protocols probe     # a subset while developing
imu-bench eval --encoder my_encoder --slurm                     # one SLURM train -> score chain per cell
imu-bench eval --encoder my_encoder --force                     # rerun cells that already have a result
imu-bench eval --encoder my_encoder --dry-run                   # list what would run

Each cell trains with the task card's recipe and scores the selected checkpoint once:

Artefact Path run directory (checkpoints, logs) runs/bench_<task>__<encoder>__<protocol>__s42/ generated config bench/generated/configs/bench_<task>__<encoder>__<protocol>__s42.yaml result file bench/results/<task>/<encoder>__<protocol>__s42.json

Model selection uses the validation split only; the evaluation split is scored once, by the task's scorer in bench/score/. The primary seed is 42 for every row of the leaderboard.

docs.title: Protocols
docs.text:
Protocol Encoder Decoder Enters the ranking probe frozen the card's light decoder, trained yes finetune trainable, from the pretrained weights the same decoder yes scratch trainable, random init the same decoder reference row

The decoders are deliberately light: a linear head for classification, width-192 attention decoders with one to four layers for the kinematic tasks, a projection for retrieval. The paper shows that a deeper decoder narrows or reverses the measured advantage of pretraining, which is why decoder capacity is part of the card and not of the submission.

docs.title: Checking a submission
docs.text:
imu-bench check my_encoder

reports whether all twenty cells exist, whether every trained config is identical to its task card (decoder, learning rate, budget, split, selection rule), whether the card is complete (name, params_m, pretrain_data, normalize_method) and which track the submission qualifies for. A cell that changed the recipe is listed outside the ranking.

docs.title: Reading results
docs.text:
imu-bench leaderboard            # bench/leaderboard_tracks.json + the two track tables

A row is shown only when all ten tasks are scored under both protocols. Rows are ordered by mean rank over the seven columns (arm pose, full-body pose, odometry, gesture, IMU–text, Parkinson's, mean activity F1 over the four sets); ties share a rank, the best value per column is marked at the printed precision, and reference rows (control_random, control_raw, scratch, released external models) are printed but never ranked. The format of a result file is in Result files.

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text: Four steps from a clone to a first scored cell.

docs.title: 1. Install and point the harness at your data
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/SPICExLAB/IMU-Bench && cd IMU-Bench
python -m venv imu-bench && source imu-bench/bin/activate && pip install -e .
export IMUBENCH_DATA_ROOT=/data/imubench      # layout in Datasets
imu-bench tasks

docs.title: 2. Run a reference encoder on one task
docs.text:
imu-bench eval --encoder control_random --tasks har_hhar --protocols probe

control_random is the shared backbone with random weights, never trained: the number it reaches is what the decoder alone achieves. The cell writes runs/bench_har_hhar__control_random__probe__s42/ and bench/results/har_hhar/control_random__probe__s42.json.

docs.title: 3. Run InrtlWrist through the plugin interface
docs.text:
imu-bench eval --encoder examples/plugin/inrtlwrist_plugin.yaml --tasks har_hhar pd_pads --protocols probe

The card points at the released checkpoint on the Hugging Face Hub; the harness downloads it. The scores should match the released result files for these cells, which verifies the data preparation.

docs.title: 4. Run your own encoder
docs.text:
Copy examples/plugin/inrtlwrist_plugin.py and .yaml, replace the model, then:

imu-bench eval --encoder my_encoder.yaml            # all ten tasks, both protocols
imu-bench check my_encoder                           # complete? protocol-faithful? which track?
imu-bench package my_encoder --out submission/       # ready for the leaderboard pull request

Details: Submission modes, Evaluation, Tracks and leaderboard submission.

docs.title: Tables and figures
docs.text:
Every table and figure is generated from the result files:

python paper_results/build.py                          # every table (.tex), figure and tidy CSV
python analysis/paper_tables/make_main_table.py        # main results table
python analysis/paper_tables/make_task_tables.py       # per-task appendix tables
python analysis/plot_main_radar.py                     # radar figure
python analysis/plot_transferability_5src.py           # cross-task transfer heatmaps

paper_results/ holds the tidy CSVs behind each element with the source file of every number.

docs.title: Pretraining InrtlWrist
docs.text:
python scripts/run_pretrain.py --config configs/base.yaml \
    --model-config configs/vit1d_ssl_mae_varlen_altattn_realdata_ocdetect_eatingspeed_motionx_sonic_flu.yaml \
    --run-name vit1d_ssl_mae_varlen_altattn_realdata_ocdetect_eatingspeed_motionx_sonic

The five controlled-track baselines use the same corpus and backbone with scripts/run_ssl_baseline.py; their configs and launch scripts are under configs/ and launch/pretrain/. The released checkpoint (144,000 updates) is on the Hub and loads with scripts/load_inrtlwrist.py:

from huggingface_hub import hf_hub_download
from scripts.load_inrtlwrist import load_inrtlwrist, zscore
enc = load_inrtlwrist(hf_hub_download("YiquanLi/InrtlWrist", "inrtlwrist_mae_5src_step144k.pt"))

docs.title: Running a cell without the CLI
docs.text:
python -m bench.make_config --task pd_pads --encoder mae_5src --protocol probe --seed 42
python scripts/run_pretrain.py --config configs/base.yaml \
    --model-config bench/generated/configs/bench_pd_pads__mae_5src__probe__s42.yaml \
    --run-name bench_pd_pads__mae_5src__probe__s42
python -m bench.score --task pd_pads --encoder mae_5src --protocol probe --seed 42

docs.title: Qualitative figures
docs.text: scripts/vis_site_pose.py and scripts/vis_site_odometry.py draw the skeleton and trajectory figures of the website from the fine-tuned checkpoints and the scorer's own reconstruction.

docs.title: Submission modes
docs.text: A cell is one task × encoder × protocol × seed. The task card fixes the raw input (one wrist, six channels in a forward–left–up frame at 50 Hz, the windows, the splits), the decoder, the recipe, the selection rule and the scorer. The encoder is the only free part, and there are two ways to supply one.

docs.title: Encoder plugin
docs.text:
Any PyTorch module can be evaluated. Write a builder and describe the encoder in a card.

# my_package/imubench.py
import torch, torch.nn as nn

class MyEncoder(nn.Module):
    embed_dim = 768                       # required: an integer attribute

    def forward(self, x):                 # x: [B, C, T] float; acc x/y/z (m/s²) then gyro x/y/z (rad/s); card's model_hz
        ...
        return {"tokens": tokens,         # [B, N, D] over time: read by the pose and odometry decoders
                "pooled": pooled}         # [B, D]: read by the classification and retrieval heads
        # returning only [B, D], or only [B, N, D], is also accepted

def build(weights=None, **kwargs) -> nn.Module:
    model = MyEncoder(**kwargs)
    if weights:
        model.load_state_dict(torch.load(weights, map_location="cpu"))
    return model

# my_encoder.yaml: one encoder per file, the key is the encoder id
my_encoder:
  name: My encoder (Doe et al., 2026)
  external_encoder: plugin
  entry: my_package.imubench:build          # imported once per job; the clone root is on sys.path
  weights: hf://my-org/my-model/encoder.pt  # or a local path
  channels: 6                               # 3 for accelerometer-only models
  model_hz: 50                              # the harness resamples the 50 Hz input to this rate
  acc_units: m/s2                           # or g
  normalize_method: zscore                  # zscore | physical | raw, applied before your model
  params_m: 85
  pretrain_data: Capture-24 (all), UK Biobank (train)    # the exact corpus, for the overlap audit
  weights_url: https://huggingface.co/my-org/my-model
  track: open

What the harness does around your model:

  • resamples to model_hz (anti-aliased polyphase filter when downsampling, linear interpolation when upsampling);
  • converts accelerometer units when acc_units: g;
  • drops the gyroscope when channels: 3;
  • applies normalize_method to the raw window;
  • for models that return a single vector, repeats it over the token grid so that the kinematic decoders still run (such a row is scored on every task, with that limitation visible in the result file).

examples/plugin/inrtlwrist_plugin.{py,yaml} wraps the reference encoder through this interface and reproduces its native scores; copy it as a template. The full contract is in imu_lm/models/baselines/plugin_encoder.py.

docs.title: Built-in architectures
docs.text: An encoder trained with this repository's trainer (the shared ViT1D of the controlled track) is registered with a run directory or checkpoint instead of a plugin entry; the cards of the released encoders in bench/registry/encoders.yaml show the fields. This is the path for controlled-track submissions, where the backbone and the corpus are fixed and only the pretraining objective differs. See Reproducing the paper for the pretraining command.

docs.title: Embeddings instead of an encoder
docs.text:
Not supported, by design:

  • the fine-tune protocol needs the encoder's weights;
  • the pose and odometry decoders need per-patch tokens, not one vector per window;
  • a frozen-probe-only entry would be ranked against rows that ran both protocols.

If the weights cannot be made public, release them to the maintainers privately with the submission. A frozen-probe-only embeddings mode for the global tasks, listed outside the ranking, is on the roadmap.

docs.title: Tracks
docs.text:
Both tracks use the same task cards, protocols and scorers; they differ in what the encoder may be.

Controlled trackOpen track

With the corpus and the model held fixed, which pretraining objective gives the most useful representation?

  • Pretrain only on the released corpus: 197,094 unlabeled wrist windows built with scripts/build_multidata_cache.py from the sources listed in Datasets.
  • Use the shared backbone (12-layer, width-384 ViT over 0.32 s patches, 21 M parameters) and the shared pretraining trainer (scripts/run_pretrain.py).
  • At most 160,000 pretraining updates, checkpoint selected on the corpus validation split.
  • Only the objective (loss, views, masking, heads discarded after pretraining) is free.

What is the best wrist-IMU encoder that anyone can train or download, at any scale?

  • Any architecture, size, pretraining corpus and objective.
  • Weights must be public, or released with the submission.
  • The pretraining corpus must not contain any recording from the evaluation splits of the ten tasks; declare it in the card (pretrain_data) so that it can be audited.
  • Input normalisation and other preprocessing inside the encoder are the submitter's choice (normalize_method).

docs.title: Submitting
docs.text:
Submissions are pull requests to the public results repository, the way SWE-bench collects experiments.

imu-bench check my_encoder
imu-bench package my_encoder --out submission/

package lays out results/<task>/…json, registry/my_encoder.yaml, the generated configs/ and check.json.

from huggingface_hub import HfApi
HfApi().upload_folder(repo_id="YiquanLi/IMU-Bench-results", repo_type="dataset",
                      folder_path="submission", create_pr=True, commit_message="Add my_encoder")

What happens next:

  1. We run imu-bench check on the pull request; a missing cell, a changed recipe or an incomplete card is reported on the PR.
  2. We check the declared pretraining corpus against the evaluation sets (Data audit and leakage). A row whose corpus contains evaluation recordings is listed as overlap and left out of the ranking of the affected tasks.
  3. For open-track submissions with public weights we re-run a sample of cells; a mismatch beyond the printed precision is reported on the PR.
  4. After merging, the leaderboard on the website and in the Space is regenerated from the merged files.

Partial submissions

imu-bench package --allow-incomplete is accepted; the row appears in the per-task tables and is ranked once all twenty cells exist.

docs.title: CLI
docs.text:
imu-bench is installed by pip install -e . (entry point bench.cli:main).

Command Does imu-bench tasks lists the ten task cards: dataset, split, input, metric imu-bench eval --encoder <id or card.yaml> [--tasks …] [--protocols probe finetune] [--seed 42] [--slurm] [--force] [--dry-run] registers a card file under bench/registry/encoders.d/, then trains and scores every requested cell, here or as SLURM chains imu-bench check <id> completeness (20 cells), protocol fidelity (trained configs identical to the task cards), card completeness, track eligibility imu-bench package <id> [--out submission] [--allow-incomplete] lays out results/, registry/<id>.yaml, configs/ and check.json for the leaderboard pull request imu-bench leaderboard [--site index.html] [--readme README.md] [--quiet] regenerates bench/leaderboard_tracks.json and the two track tables; optionally rewrites the website and README blocks imu-bench audit <dir> --subject-regex '<pattern>' [--glob '**/*.csv'] [--acc-cols AccX AccY AccZ] [--threshold 0.999] finds duplicated, mirrored or rotated participants in a dataset release imu-bench fetch-weights [ids…] downloads the released weights of the open-track models to where their cards expect them

The lower-level modules remain available: python -m bench.make_config, python -m bench.launch, python -m bench.score, python -m bench.leaderboard (see Reproducing the paper).

Environment variables:

Variable Meaning IMUBENCH_DATA_ROOT directory holding the datasets in the layout of Datasets; every dataset path in the cards is rewritten to it IMUBENCH_VENV environment directory activated by generated SLURM scripts (default imu-bench/) BENCH_PARTITION, BENCH_ACCOUNT SLURM partition and account for --slurm

docs.title: Encoder cards
docs.text: An encoder card is a YAML mapping with one key, the encoder id. Cards of the released encoders are in bench/registry/encoders.yaml; cards registered with imu-bench eval --encoder <file> go to bench/registry/encoders.d/<id>.yaml.

docs.title: Fields
docs.text: Field Required Meaning name yes display name, with the reference params_m yes parameter count in millions pretrain_data yes the pretraining corpus, dataset by dataset with the split used (audited against the evaluation sets) normalize_method yes zscore (per channel and window), physical (m/s² and rad/s as stored) or raw; applied by the harness before the encoder, identically in every cell channels yes 6 (accelerometer + gyroscope) or 3 (accelerometer only) track yes open or controlled external_encoder plugin / adapters plugin for the plugin interface; harnet, normwear, inertia1 … for the built-in adapters entry plugin package.module:build; build(weights=<path or None>, **kwargs) returns an nn.Module with an integer embed_dim weights plugin local path, hf://<org>/<repo>/<file> (downloaded with huggingface_hub), or builtin kwargs plugin keyword arguments passed to build model_hz plugin sampling rate the model expects; the harness resamples from 50 Hz acc_units plugin m/s2 (default) or g weights_url open track where the weights are published run, ckpt built-in run directory under runs/ and checkpoint name (best, latest, …) for encoders trained with this repository's trainer alt_attention, shared_kernel, use_cls built-in architecture flags of the shared ViT1D preprocess_from built-in pretraining config whose preprocessing the cells inherit group, order, short, hide_in_summary optional display metadata for the tables

docs.title: Plugin contract
docs.text:
def build(weights=None, **kwargs) -> torch.nn.Module   # attribute embed_dim: int
module(x)   # x: [B, C, T] float at model_hz; acc x/y/z then gyro x/y/z, wrist FLU frame
            # -> {"tokens": [B, N, D], "pooled": [B, D]}, or only [B, N, D], or only [B, D]

tokens are read by the pose and odometry decoders on the harness grid of T // 16 patches (0.32 s at 50 Hz); pooled is read by the classification and retrieval heads. A model that returns only a pooled vector is repeated over the token grid; a model that returns only tokens is mean-pooled. See examples/plugin/inrtlwrist_plugin.py.

docs.title: Result files
docs.text:
One JSON per cell at bench/results/<task>/<encoder>__<protocol>__s<seed>.json, written by the task's scorer:

{
  "task": "microgesture_openwatch",
  "encoder": "mae_5src",
  "protocol": "probe",
  "seed": 42,
  "metrics": {"clip_macro_f1": 0.647, "clip_acc": 0.678, "window_macro_f1": 0.494, "window_acc": 0.536},
  "primary_metric": "clip_macro_f1",
  "eval_split": "test",
  "run": "bench_microgesture_openwatch__mae_5src__probe__s42",
  "checkpoint": "runs/.../checkpoints/best.pt",
  "checkpoint_step": 1200,
  "selection": {"split": "val", "monitor": "macro_f1", "mode": "max"},
  "job_ids": [7212525],
  "provenance": {"legacy_run": false, "scorer": "bench.score.microgesture", "scored_at": "..."},
  "status": "ok",
  "notes": "",
  "schema_version": 1
}
Field Meaning metrics every metric the scorer computes; the leaderboard reads primary_metric eval_split test where a test split exists (gesture, retrieval), otherwise the held-out validation split the card defines checkpoint_step the step selected by the card's rule on the validation split provenance scorer, time, and whether the run predates the harness (legacy_run)

imu-bench leaderboard collects these files into bench/leaderboard_tracks.json (per track and protocol: rows, cells, ranks) and the Markdown/HTML tables. The released result files, the registry and the leaderboard data are mirrored in the dataset YiquanLi/IMU-Bench-results, whose results_long.csv lists every cell as one row.

docs.title: Task cards
docs.text:
bench/registry/tasks.yaml holds one card per task: dataset and split rule, input window, output and decoder, optimisation recipe per protocol, selection rule, metrics with their direction, scorer. imu-bench tasks prints the summary. The ten tasks of the benchmark:

Task id Dataset Input window Output Primary metric Split arm_pose_nymeria Nymeria, real right-wrist IMU + mocap 10.24 s, 50 Hz 5 right-arm joint rotations per 0.32 s position error, cm ↓ recording session full_body_pose_nymeria Nymeria 10.24 s 23 SMPL joint rotations per 0.32 s root-relative MPJPE, mm ↓ recording session odometry_nymeria_local Nymeria 2.56 s pelvis velocity in the wrist frame, integrated ATE, m ↓ recording session microgesture_openwatch OpenWatch (43 canonical identities) 1 s, 100 Hz 5 gestures + background, voted per clip clip macro-F1 ↑ subject, posture-stratified language_humanml3d HumanML3D, simulated wrist IMU 10.24 s alignment with CLIP ViT-B/32 text mean Recall@1, galleries of 100 ↑ official test split pd_pads PADS (469 participants) 2.56 s healthy / Parkinson's / differential per participant participant macro-F1 ↑ subject-disjoint 80/20 har_hhar HHAR (6 classes) 2.56 s window label macro-F1 ↑ subject-disjoint har_mhealth MHEALTH (12) 2.56 s window label macro-F1 ↑ subject-disjoint har_prism PrISM (5 global classes) 2.56 s window label macro-F1 ↑ subject-disjoint har_userwatch TransfHAR (60) 2.56 s window label macro-F1 ↑ 80/20 in time per recording

Every input is one wrist, accelerometer x/y/z (m/s², gravity included) then gyroscope x/y/z (rad/s), in a forward–left–up frame, resampled to the card's rate.

Decoders: linear heads for classification; width-192 attention decoders with two cross-channel and two temporal layers for arm pose, one cross-channel layer for full-body pose and one temporal layer for odometry; a projection into the CLIP text space for retrieval. Classification heads are trained with inverse-frequency class-weighted cross-entropy. The activity column of the leaderboard is the mean macro-F1 over the four activity sets.

Other task ids in tasks.yaml (decoder ladders, rotation variants, the release split of OpenWatch, world-frame odometry, extra activity sets) are ablations and controls from the paper; they are marked disabled and need --allow-disabled in bench.launch.
